**Summary — all 44 units categorized, each with independent git+PR evidence (not trusting task.yaml's branch field):**

- **CAT1 (26, safe to archive)** — 0 unique commits vs origin/master, 0 dirty, no PR. Includes the 8-task "phase7-vericomposer" cluster (7 already ancestors of master), the pr79-work branch (content already merged via PR #79, confirmed by `merge-base --is-ancestor`), and 17 rca-* tasks whose real branches turned out to be plain stale checkouts of master with zero unique work.

- **CAT3 (9, do-not-touch, open PR)** — tied to PRs #563, #489, #578, #581, #580, #575, #576, #583, #582, all still OPEN. Two of these (`171129`, `171157`) had task.yaml branch fields pointing at an entirely different, older task — resolved by using the real upstream ref.
- **CAT4 (2, highest priority, data-loss risk)** — `task-20260726-172016-mother-router...` and `task-20260726-175954-rca-...171939...` each have exactly 1 commit that `git branch -r --contains HEAD` confirms exists on **no** remote branch anywhere — genuinely local-only.
- **CAT5 (3, needs human open-or-abandon call)** — `083946`, `182702`, `185117` each have 1 real commit vs master that **is** safely pushed to their own remote branch, but no PR was ever opened.

No files were deleted, pushed, merged, or had systemd state touched; the backup directory and all workspaces were left exactly as found.
